works.title: The Society of Tomorrow

author.name: Gustave de Molinari
author.biography: Belgian-born economist of the French liberal school, editor of the Journal des economistes for decades, and the first theorist to ask whether even security could be supplied by competition rather than monopoly.

works.description: Molinari's late forecast of a world ordered by free contract: the state of war giving way to the state of peace, written at the end of six decades of argument. The 1904 English edition, from the shelves of David Hart's Digital Library of Liberty and Power.

works.title: Common Sense

author.name: Thomas Paine
author.biography: English corset-maker turned American revolutionary pamphleteer. Common Sense, published anonymously in January 1776, made the case for independence in language a dockworker could quote, and sold in numbers no American publication had approached.

works.description: The pamphlet that turned a colonial tax dispute into an argument for independence, in the first-edition text of January 1776. Originally English; from the shelves of David Hart's Digital Library of Liberty and Power.

works.title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations

author.name: Adam Smith
author.biography: Scottish moral philosopher of the Glasgow chair and the Kirkcaldy study. The Wealth of Nations of 1776 organized a century of scattered economic argument into the founding book of political economy.

works.description: The founding book of political economy, in Edwin Cannan's scholarly edition of 1904. Originally English; from the shelves of David Hart's Digital Library of Liberty and Power.

works.title: Principles of Political Economy

author.name: John Stuart Mill
author.biography: Philosopher, economist and member of Parliament, raised on Bentham and Ricardo and educated past both. His Principles ruled the teaching of economics in English for half a century.

works.description: The textbook of classical political economy in its author's final text, the seventh edition of 1871. Originally English; from the shelves of David Hart's Digital Library of Liberty and Power.
